questions.question: What is the core end-to-end invariant of the lesson?
options: Keep input identity, representation version, model version, and decision policy connected to the outcome
Always use the largest available language model
Normalize every language with one universal rule
Return a model score without product policy
questions.explanation: A production decision is reproducible only when its input and every compatible transformation and policy version remain connected.

questions.question: A service receives 200 requests per second and each request schedules 600 tokens. What is the admitted token demand?
questions.explanation: Token demand is requests per second multiplied by scheduled tokens per request: 200 x 600 = 120,000 tokens/s.

questions.question: Why can increasing maximum batch wait break an otherwise efficient online service?
options: The wait consumes the same end-to-end deadline needed by preprocessing, queueing, inference, and policy
questions.explanation: Batching may improve throughput, but waiting for a fuller batch directly reduces remaining latency headroom.

questions.question: A tokenizer replica emits IDs from an older vocabulary to a newly deployed model. What is the correct first response?
options: Stop the incompatible bundle rollout and restore a matched tokenizer-model version
Average the old and new token IDs
questions.explanation: This is a semantic compatibility failure, not a transient transport error. Retrying or waiting cannot make mismatched IDs correct.

questions.question: Why does the batching example budget tokens instead of only counting requests?
options: NLP requests can have very different sequence lengths and therefore very different work and memory cost
Every request contains exactly one token
Request count is unavailable to a scheduler
Token budgets guarantee perfect model quality
questions.explanation: A request-count limit can still admit one or more unusually long sequences and exceed the intended compute or memory envelope.

questions.question: The global accuracy improves, but accuracy for long Arabic documents falls below its release threshold. What should the gate do?
options: Block promotion and investigate the affected slice
Promote because the global average improved
questions.explanation: Averages can hide regressions that materially harm one workload slice; explicit slice thresholds make that failure visible and actionable.

questions.question: Which signal best reveals that requests are waiting too long before model execution?
questions.explanation: Queue age measures how long admitted work waits and directly exposes deadline pressure that accelerator utilization alone can hide.
